title: I made a browser-based CoD Zombies Der Riese Tribute with Opus 5 (solo & co-op, free)
author: yerbamate2020
selftext:
Last weekend I made a browser-based zombies game (inspired by Der Riese from CoD World at War) fully with AI (Kimi K3). It [came out alright](https://x.com/0xRishi/status/2080024077662847030), but was very blocky-looking, muted and not polished.  
  
This past weekend, I did a [visual overhaul of the game with Opus 5](https://x.com/0xRishi/status/2081230708593590378), which completely changed the look and feel of the game (video demo attached).  
  
**The entire map, all weapons, every interactive machine (pack-a-punch, perk machines, mystery box, teleporters, doors), sky, particles, muzzle flashes were generated with code - NOT pre-made assets.** The game runs on Three.js and has multiplayer functionality with voice chat. The sound effects were fully generated with ElevenLabs SFX + Voice Design/TTS for the characters.  
  
Hundreds of people have already played it around the world. It's incredible what someone who just loves games but has no game-development experience can do now!  
  
**You can play it for free at** [**derkoloss.com**](http://derkoloss.com)**!**   
  
I've also [open-sourced the codebase](https://github.com/rishipr/der-koloss-ce) (which contains a lot of interesting tidbits in the README) and uploaded 28 minutes of raw multiplayer footage [here](https://x.com/0xRishi/status/2082219953667846618) for anyone interested :)

comments.author: Imaginary-Can6136
comments.body:
Looks absolutely sick!

I’ll be feeding my Claude your codebase, I’ll play it as soon as I get a minute

I see that you are missing hands/arms: I’ve had a shocking amount of trouble creating hands/arms in 1st person shooters I’m working on.

Did you run into issues as well?

replies.author: yerbamate2020
replies.body:
Thanks man and awesome to hear!

The zombies have all the body parts (those were one of the few things that came from a CC0 asset bundle); the soldiers were generated by Opus with code and was the hardest parts to nail for the model. It took a lot of revisions and was very rough, but the characters do finally have very primitive arms/hands holding the guns when you look in multiplayer. 

You can check out the latest full soldier models at the tweet below, which also includes the first iteration which was ***much*** rougher

[https://x.com/0xRishi/status/2082219953667846618](https://x.com/0xRishi/status/2082219953667846618)

replies.author: Imaginary-Can6136
replies.body:
Thanks for the reference!

Why do you think arms are so tough?

I haven’t actually asked Claude (it’s down rn so idk what to do with my life)

It seems like something that would’ve been much simpler than a lot of the other stuff I’ve seen it do, but there must be something tricky about it

replies.author: yerbamate2020
replies.body:
To be honest I have no idea! I haven't yet experimented with "image to 3d" / "text to 3d" models like Tripo and Meshy but that's next up on my list.

FWIW, here's the answer from Claude when I asked it in my repo:

*A gun is one shape, so I build it, look at it, and it's done. A body has to look right in every pose, from every angle, at every moment of every movement, and one bad moment is enough to look broken. The maths that puts a hand in the right place says nothing about which way the wrist is twisted, so everything measured perfect while the arm was on backwards. The body is also solid pieces bolted to a skeleton rather than skin that stretches, so bending a joint too far pulls the shoulder open, and my own measuring tools kept calling all of it fine.*

All that being said, I don't think this will be a problem a year from now (or even sooner) - which is super exciting! My guess is all the big model providers are focusing in a material way on game development/creation as a core capability of the models. Wrote a bit about why here in case interested: [https://x.com/0xRishi/status/2081852360037654761](https://x.com/0xRishi/status/2081852360037654761)

comments.author: AlberionLive
comments.body:
What's your solution for multiplayer? Are you hosting on a personal server? Have you run into any capacity issues?

I'm working on a multiplayer game playable via browser and I've got it hosted on my own server, but I'm wondering at what point I should start looking at P2P networking.

replies.author: yerbamate2020
replies.body:
There's a section on how multiplayer works in the repo's README here: [https://github.com/rishipr/der-koloss-ce#multiplayer](https://github.com/rishipr/der-koloss-ce#multiplayer)  
  
Tl;dr - no personal server, so no capacity issues. All runs P2P on a single host per lobby, and each lobby is limited to 4 players which this model can run no problem.

No host migration logic set up atm, so if the host leaves, then the game ends - but I'd think host migration logic wouldn't be that tough to set up in such a model. Clients (guests) can of course leave the game without any disruption to other players.

replies.author: AlberionLive
replies.body:
Thanks for the repo link!  
  
Have you gotten any feedback from players finding issues unable to connect? 

I asked claude to look at the differences between what you set up and what I've tried; it wanted me to ask if you're using a PeerServer broker that you're self-hosting, or using the free public cloud broker.

I tried using webRTC but struggled with lobbies over 4 players, which you've nicely capped your game at.

replies.author: AlberionLive
replies.body: Cheers - thanks for the replies! This is definitely a fun space to dev in, and browser first removes a lot of barriers to play.

replies.author: AlberionLive
replies.body:
Not sure if you're looking for playtest feedback, but on the first level, there's a long wide platform.

If you stand on the side of the platform (near the gates), and try to shoot onto the platform, the bullets hit an invisible wall, and aren't able to hit enemies.

Overall the UI looks great and your repo is really clean too.

replies.author: yerbamate2020
replies.body:
Appreciate the feedback! Hadn't caught that from our own playthroughs but will fix it shortly.  
  
Appreciate the kind words :) LMK if you end up cooking anything in the space and are down to share - would love to see!
